paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. This song asks for a blessing, and the blessing is never the end of the line. It says, "May God be gracious to us and bless us…" so that "Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations." (Psalm 67:1-2) The blessing is a delivery truck, friend, and you are not the final stop.

And look who the song keeps calling on: "Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You." (Psalm 67:3, 5) All the peoples, said twice, in case somebody in the back was checking their phone. The song says the nations can "be glad and sing for joy," because "You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth." (Psalm 67:4) God's heart is big enough for the whole world, so yours can be too.

So what do you do with it, baker? When you get a good harvest, a good week or a good day, treat it as God blessing you so His ways get known. The song ends right there: "God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him." (Psalm 67:7) Take what He gives you, say thank you, and then pass it on, like a cookie box you were never meant to keep all to yourself.
